status: partial adaptation; no acceptance inferred from export or component checks
notes: Rows use matching requested component formats; source and actual tensor types are separately recorded. HiFT always stores F32. Vision component export is F32.
CPU kernels use F32 accumulation, with weight-format-specific prepared input QDQ. Thinker KV F32/F16 and talker KV F32 are separate from weight storage.
Auto is implemented through shared dispatch but actual CPU/GPU execution and submission counts must be measured per entrypoint; an Auto fallback is not GPU support.
Entrypoint states identify their measured artifact in entrypoint-results.json; they are functional checks, distinct from component numerical acceptance. Untested combinations remain not run.
Unsupported complete Vulkan is not implemented, rather than not applicable. Remaining model/session and shared-device layers are specified in validation.md.

The earlier claim that shared Qwen3-VL/DeepStack Vulkan support was absent is corrected: the current shared decoder already implements it. Actual model/backend validation is still required; audio and HiFT device gaps remain separate.

Grouped CLI text/image/audio reuses the shared grouped core and configured resident runtime. HTTP grouped text/image is implemented; audio HTTP retains its existing single schema. Local handler tests do not establish model matrix passes.

Historical mmproj-F32.gguf stored F32 but used Q8-prepacked aligned linears and dynamic Q8 inputs, with F32 fallback for the 4304-wide FFN-down input. Those image entrypoint passes remain historical functional evidence; new lossless image CLI/HTTP and single/grouped JEV have not been rerun.

Mixed-format audio/S2S measurements have separate rows and do not establish an all-Q8 component configuration. Prior Auto CPU fallback used the older width-cap gate; the reviewed strict device run reaches Vulkan and fails the unchanged numerical model contract.

New vision-lossless-mmproj-F32.gguf explicitly sets boolean clip.vision.preserve_f32=true, preserving F32 linear weights/activations through the existing lossless path. Missing/false metadata and existing WeVisOne compatibility retain previous behavior. The 352 tensor payloads and original metadata match the historical asset.

Independent official Transformers 4.57.6 CPU/four-thread vision-only execution passes 32/32 checkpoints for the fixed red image, with unchanged F32 gates rRMSE <= 0.001 and cosine >= 0.999999. Direct encoder checks do not establish new lossless CLI/HTTP or Auto/Vulkan acceptance. Vision tower rows use kv=none because the encoder has no KV cache.

The historical Sophon shared-default vision asset has identical projected and three DeepStack plane hashes before/after the opt-in change. Other models' real vision assets were unavailable; their real vision regressions remain unverified.

Latest CPU image entrypoints use explicit clip.vision.preserve_f32=true, with Q8_0 thinker/F16 KV. All nine checks pass, including CLI/HTTP probability equality. The direct independent vision Oracle passes 32/32; combined-model numerical/task-quality acceptance remains separate.

Final Auto text HTTP and CLI fallback checks pass after real device submissions. A genuine second-chunk device loss in 68-token HTTP JEV now replays the entire current input and matches CPU probabilities exactly; original pre-fix difference 0.02338428422808647 is retained. Strict Vulkan numerical failure remains a separate failed acceptance row.
